clue.text: Lawrence's work as artist in part of London

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the standard abbreviation for an artist
Bow is a district in the East End of London

explanation.surface: Someone describes a novelist's paintings being shown in a corner of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: D. H. Lawrence wrote the novel The Rainbow; the clue's 'work' is a book, not a painting. BOW is a district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rainbow is a 1915 novel by D. H. Lawrence, so it is one of his works.

clue.text: Extra clause about a thief

indicators.note: the word for an extra clause goes round the letter a

parts.note: a rider is a clause added to a document or bill

explanation.surface: A contract gets an added clause concerning a robber.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider attacks to steal, so is a kind of robber.

clue.text: Thick paint in pots I am getting mixed

indicators.note: the words pots, I and am are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist mixes up thick paint in the tins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting mixed' rearranges POTS I AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is paint laid on so thickly that brush or knife marks stand out.

clue.text: Study of vegetation on tree in Australian place

parts.note: botany is the science of plants
the bay is a laurel tree

explanation.surface: Researching plants on a tree somewhere in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany Bay is an inlet at Sydney where Captain Cook landed in 1770.

clue.text: Funds obtained from somewhere with a loan

indicators.note: obtained from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Money raised from some place along with a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: The wherewithal is the money or means needed for a purpose.

clue.text: Supports what people have when annoyed

explanation.surface: A note on the things people get when they are irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: To back up is to support someone; an angry person is said to have their back up, like a bristling cat.

clue.text: Pace bowler's intended victim

parts.note: in cricket a fast bowler aims to beat the willow blade held by the person facing him

explanation.surface: A fast cricket bowler sizes up the batsman he means to dismiss.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a pace bowler is a fast bowler; he aims to get past the blade in the batsman's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The fast bowler tries to beat the blade the batsman holds, so the bowling targets that wooden club.

clue.text: College poet

explanation.surface: A university college and a verse writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Clare is a Cambridge college, and John Clare was a 19th-century English rural versifier.

clue.text: Ordered rum, as in part of South America

indicators.note: ordered means put into a fresh arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker asks for rum while in a South American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' rearranges RUM AS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Surinam, now Suriname, is a country on the north coast of South America.

clue.text: Missile from West to East split between North and South?

parts.note: Polaris was a submarine-launched nuclear missile
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A rocket fired across the map divides the two poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from West to' just says the missile is followed by E, read left to right.
explanation.definitionFit: To polarise is to divide into two opposing extremes, like the two poles of the earth.

clue.text: Intimate quiet can make you restless

indicators.note: the letters of the words before can be rearranged to make a new word

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: A close but silent companion leaves you fidgety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' rearranges INTIMATE plus P into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless cannot wait calmly, which is the state of being eager and unwilling to wait.

clue.text: Leader of female trio appearing annually

definitions.text: Leader of female trio appearing annually

parts.words: Leader of female trio appearing annually
parts.note: three consecutive months of the calendar are also girls' names, and this month comes first of them every year

explanation.surface: The front woman of a girl group turns up once a year.
explanation.walkthrough: The three months April, May and June are all women's names; the first of them leads that trio each year.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month is followed by May and June, all three also used as girls' names, so it heads that trio.

clue.text: You'll find here no West German city

definitions.text: You'll find here no West German city

parts.words: You'll find here no West German city
parts.note: the city's name is spelt only with compass points, south, south, east and north, and has no letter for west

explanation.surface: A traveller is told a certain city is not in West Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'West' as the compass letter W: the name is made of the compass letters E, S, S, E, N with no W, yet it was a West German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, in what was West Germany when this was set.

clue.text: Oriental author's divided attention

indicators.note: the author's name splits the word for attention into two parts

parts.note: to give ear is to give attention
Laurence Sterne is the author of Tristram Shandy; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A writer from Asia finds his concentration split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided' puts STERNE between EA and R of EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and easterner both describe a person from the East, especially Asia.

clue.text: All-rounders bearing seals of approval

parts.note: the round things are finger bands, each carrying an engraved device for stamping wax

explanation.surface: Versatile cricketers receive official endorsements.
explanation.walkthrough: An all-rounder is a cricketer who both bats and bowls; here it is anything round, a ring, carrying a seal.
explanation.definitionFit: These finger bands carry an engraved seal used to stamp wax on documents as a mark of authority.

clue.text: Performing outside but odd poet is a sceptic

indicators.note: the word for performing goes round the scrambled word but

parts.note: doing a play is performing it

indicators.note: odd signals the word but is rearranged strangely

parts.note: Dylan Thomas was the Welsh poet

explanation.surface: An eccentric poet acting out of doors is a sceptic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' turns BUT into UBT, and 'outside' puts DOING round it; then add Dylan THOMAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Thomas would not believe in the Resurrection without proof, so his name became an idiom for any doubter.

clue.text: Top-class performer raised a sort of rifle

parts.note: something raised is high

indicators.note: a sort of signals the word rifle is rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A star turn lifts a kind of gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges RIFLE into FLIER. The grid as filed reads HIGHPLIER, an OCR misreading of F.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-flier is someone extremely successful or ambitious, an outstanding achiever.

clue.text: Tittle-tattle from nasty gossip about couple

indicators.note: the word for a nasty gossip goes round the word for couple

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful, gossiping woman
to hitch is to couple or join, as a trailer to a car

explanation.surface: Idle talk from a spiteful gossip concerning a pair of lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HITCH inside CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tittle-tattle and chitchat are both light, idle gossip.

clue.text: King mated with or without help of bishops

definitions.text: King mated with or without help of bishops

parts.words: King mated with or without help of bishops
parts.note: reads like a chess checkmate, but describes a monarch who married six times, sometimes with the Church's blessing and sometimes after breaking with Rome

explanation.surface: A chess king is checkmated, perhaps using bishops, perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: 'mated' means married, and the bishops are churchmen who did or did not sanction the Tudor king's marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor monarch married six wives, some with Church approval and some after his break with Rome.

clue.text: A king once more rises and falls

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: R, rex, is the abbreviation for a king
again means once more

explanation.surface: A monarch climbs back up and tumbles down again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' reverses A + R + AGAIN in this down clue to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US-Canada border, so it is a set of falls.

clue.text: Get exercised about king and country

indicators.note: the word for getting exercise goes round the royal letters

parts.note: to train is to exercise or get exercise
ER, Edwardus Rex, is a royal cipher for King Edward

explanation.surface: Someone gets worked up over the monarch and the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ER inside TRAIN; 'Get exercised' looks like getting angry, but means training.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land with its physical features, which is country in the landscape sense.

clue.text: This VIP may be said to smile

definitions.text: This VIP may be said to smile

parts.words: This VIP may be said to smile
parts.note: an important person is a big one of these, and photographers ask you to say it so you smile

explanation.surface: A dignitary might be asked to grin for the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: Two idioms: a VIP is a 'big' one, and photographers tell their subjects to say it to make them smile.
explanation.definitionFit: A VIP is called a big cheese, and saying the word makes your mouth smile for photographs.

clue.text: Representative who should be broad-minded?

parts.note: a sales representative on the road, playing on the saying that travel broadens the mind

explanation.surface: A sales rep is expected to have a tolerant outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: A commercial traveller is an old term for a travelling sales representative; the saying 'travel broadens the mind' supplies the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller is a sales rep who journeys around, and travel proverbially broadens the mind.

clue.text: Government leader in new-type republic

indicators.note: the first letter of government goes inside the rearranged word
new signals the word type is made over in a fresh order
leader means the first letter of the word government

explanation.surface: A head of government stands in a new kind of republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns TYPE into EYPT, and 'in' puts G (the leader of 'Government') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a nation in north-east Africa governed as a republic since 1953.

clue.text: Out after three, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the position after third in a sequence is fourth

explanation.surface: A batsman is dismissed after scoring three.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid as filed reads PORTH, an OCR misreading of F; the clue gives FORTH, out, which sounds like FOURTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To go forth is to go out, so the two adverbs share a sense.

clue.text: Actor playing villain is hard to bear

explanation.surface: A performer cast as the bad guy is tough to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage villain is called the heavy, and a load that is hard to bear is weighty.

clue.text: "He's after an office", Frank scoffed

parts.note: candid means frank and open
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed is ate

explanation.surface: Someone named Frank mocks a person seeking promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a name and scoffed like mockery; they are an adjective and a verb of eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing for election seeks a post, which is what a nominee or applicant does.

clue.text: Short-tailed dog

indicators.note: tailed means the final letter is cut off, as a docked tail

parts.note: curt means short or brusque

explanation.surface: A dog with a docked tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailed' removes the last letter T from CURT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel or worthless dog.

clue.text: Proposer of tribute to flower

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: Someone raises a glass in honour of a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who proposes a toast at a dinner raises glasses in honour of someone.

clue.text: Foreign rum

explanation.surface: A drink from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange can mean alien or from elsewhere, and rum is British slang for odd or peculiar.
